text:
sasha: quick summary from offline replay run (prefetch-merge variant vs baseline). used tracepack v2026-03-01, ~10k traces sampled from prod-evens. saw a perf regression on long multi-turn sessions. :thinking:

mohit: numbers pls — p50/p95, token/s, cache hit?

anna: paste of the key metrics i extracted: 
- baseline (queue-sculptor v3): p50 = 78ms, p95 = 312ms, tokens/sec = 18.9k, kv-hit = 62%
- prefetch-merge (candidate): p50 = 82ms, p95 = 410ms, tokens/sec = 17.3k, kv-hit = 70%
- delta: +5% p50, +31% p95, -8.5% tokens/sec, +8pp kv-hit

anna: looks like we improved cache locality (kv-hit) but the tail latency worsened, especially for traces with >4096 ctx.

alex: interesting. do you see kernel-selection churn (i.e. switching to slower kernels for long sequences) around the tail?

anna: yes — profiler shows a jump at seq_len ~4096 where runtime picks the fallback attention kernel (slower FP16 path) more often. stack snippet from a sample trace: 
```
2026-03-09 13:12:45.123 TRACE id=tx123
  batch_size=6, seq_avg=4320, chosen_kernel="attn_fallback_kv"
  kv_hits=0.88, prefetch_merge=true
```

jamie: so prefetch-merge increases KV hits but also tends to aggregate requests into batches that cross the kernel-selection threshold, causing the slower kernel to be chosen. tradeoff.

mohit: can you show the batching histogram? are we increasing coalesced batch lengths?

anna: histogram (percentiles of batch token counts, prefetch-merge vs baseline): 
- baseline: p50=512, p90=1024, p99=2200
- prefetch-merge: p50=600, p90=1400, p99=3600

sasha: that's the smoking gun — more large batches. those big batches save token cost but trigger different kernel selection for long sequences and blow up p95.

alex: do we have a way to bias batching to avoid crossing the kernel threshold while still keeping higher kv-hit? maybe a token-budget cap per batch that stops at 4k tokens?

anna: i ran a micro-probe with token_budget_target=4096 and token_budget_soft=true: 
```json
{"prefetch_merge":true, "token_budget_target":4096, "token_budget_soft":true, "queue_policy":"latency-aware"}
```
results: p50=80ms, p95=336ms, tokens/sec=18.2k, kv-hit=68% — tail improved but not back to baseline.

mohit: can we A/B on the replay harness with a small randomized rollout on the traces that have long tails, to estimate user-visible impact? what's sample size?

replay-bot: ab-harness scheduled: groupA=baseline, groupB=prefetch-merge+soft-4096, traces=2k stratified on session-length, seed=42. estimated power for detecting 10% p95 change = 0.85. run_id=rb-218765

jamie: good. also request adding kernel-selection logging in the harness so we can correlate chosen_kernel -> p95. add fields: model_variant, seq_len, batch_token_count, chosen_kernel, kv_hit_rate.

sasha: action items: 
- anna: run ab-harness with the replay-bot config on the stratified 2k sample, attach per-trace kernel logs (ETA 8h) @anna
- alex: prototype a token_budget_hard_cap option at 4096 in the batching runtime to test behavior under enforced cap (ETA tomorrow) @alex
- mohit: review kernel-selection thresholds with backend team; check if we can shift the boundary or add a lightweight kernel for the 4k-6k regime (ETA 48h) @mohit

anna: one more note — the sim uncovered a micro-regression in the continuous-batcher codepath: when prefetch_merge=true we do an extra atomic compare-exchange per request that shows up in CPU profile and may increase queueing latency under high QPS. i'll include flamegraphs in the run artifact.

mohit: thanks. if the ab shows user-impact we should revert prefetch-merge or deploy the soft token cap by default.

sasha: agree. schedule a follow-up sync tomorrow 10:30 PST with eng-runtime + infra-kernel folks. i'll post calendar invite. :calendar:

alex: noted, will start the cap prototype now.

anna: starting the ab now (rb-218765), will ping when artifacts uploaded. :rocket:
